memory_candidates.content: check-extension-docs.sh test fixtures that drive the script as a subprocess (EXT_DIR pointed at a synthetic extension) must resolve the script-under-test with SOURCE-STORE FIRST, deployed-tree FALLBACK -- the opposite priority from library tests like test-phase-heading-patterns.sh's deploy-first pattern. A test validating logic still landing only in the source store (not yet redeployed) will silently test a stale deployed copy and produce false negatives on every assertion if it prefers deploy-first. Confirmed empirically while building test-index-entries-schema.sh: preferring .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh first made all 9 assertions fail until the candidate order was flipped to prefer the sibling source-store copy.

When a plan's Scope Hypothesis predicts a violation count for a new hand-written jq lint predicate (e.g. 'Rule T fires for 14 of 19 extensions'), verify the prediction's OWN enumeration completeness before assuming a mismatch means the predicate is wrong. In this task, the actual count (17) differed from the predicted count (14) not because the predicate was buggy, but because the prediction's source research only tallied one violation type (load_when.languages) and omitted a second, independent violation type (load_when.skills) that flags 3 additional extensions with zero languages usage. Always decompose an unexpected count by violation-type before concluding the code is wrong.
